assign.outcome:
**Paging hub now scrolls at its own home.** The site's leaf rule (`styles.css:297-298`) hides overflow on any `.pages` region that shows neither a `.page.active-page` nor a `.default` — the hub's home (`.paging-home`) is neither, so `.paging-app-centre` lost its scrollbar the one moment it is the leaf. One rule in `paging.css`, `.pages.paging-app-centre:not(:has(> .page.active-page)):not(:has(> .page.active-ancestor)) { overflow-y: scroll; }`, answers the site rule's own question for this region — its (0,6,0) beats the site rule's (0,4,0) outright, no load-order dependency. Reproduced and proved with a real mouse-wheel gesture, not just `el.scrollTop =` (that moves regardless of `overflow-y` per the CSSOM-view spec, so it is not proof on its own, though logged too): before the fix, a wheel over the region left `scrollTop` at 0 at both 1920 and 400; after, it reaches 400 at both. `/imagine/paging/navigation/` (a child page) still scrolls (`overflow-y: scroll`) with its home correctly hidden (`display: none`) — unaffected. Zero console errors throughout, at 1920, 400 and a 1600 doc-skill check. One Watch-out line in the readme names the trap. Nothing left open — the one-rule budget covered the whole bug.
